analyst_view.overall: Eighth-placed Stuttgart (13 points from 10 games) host seventh-placed Frankfurt (15 points) in a mid-table meeting where both want to keep pace with the European places. Stuttgart play Inter away in the Champions League on Wednesday and come into Saturday with three days' rest; midfielder Angelo Stiller, who has missed their last four games with a groin problem, travels to Italy and is expected back, while Jaquez (rib), Sauer and Diehl (both muscle) are out. Frankfurt are missing Ngankam (thigh) and have won two of their last three league games. The numbers already count Frankfurt's high recent shot volume and Stuttgart's leaky spell; no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, a high figure driven by Stuttgart's attack at home. Stiller's return should steady Stuttgart's midfield, but they lose Jaquez in defence and come off a midweek trip to Milan, so the two roughly cancel out. I stay at about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, already lifting Frankfurt (+5%) for their recent 35 corners in six games. None of the reported absences (Jaquez, Sauer, Diehl for Stuttgart, Ngankam for Frankfurt) changes either side's wide play much. I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already nudged up for both teams' busier recent card counts. No referee is named yet and the match carries no derby or extra edge beyond the race for Europe. I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots, already raising Frankfurt by almost 19% because Stuttgart allowed 107 shots in their last six. Much of that came while Stiller, the player who controls Stuttgart's midfield, was out; with him expected back, I lean slightly lower (-3%), about 29.3, though he may need easing in after Wednesday.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, already raising Frankfurt (+10%) for their recent accuracy and trimming Stuttgart slightly. Stiller's return may cut Frankfurt's chances a little, but Stuttgart's own finishing without injured attackers Sauer and Diehl is no better, so I stay at about 11.
